Stafford's population increased by around 6,000 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 140,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Stafford increased by 4.6%, from just under 130,900 in 2011 to around 136,900 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the West Midlands (6.2%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Stafford was home to around 1.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land. This area was among the lowest 25% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Stafford than across the West Midlands

An older Stafford

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Stafford increased by two years, from 43 to 45 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the West Midlands as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 75 to 84 years rose by around 3,100 (an increase of 38.9%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 3,300 (11.6% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 75 and 84 years increased by 2.0 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Changing relationships in Stafford

Stafford saw England's joint third-largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership (from 9.1% in 2011 to 10.1% in 2021).

England's largest increases in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership occurred in Richmondshire (from 8.2% to 9.4%) followed by Ryedale (from 8.7% to 9.8%).

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.7% to 8.8%, while the percentage in nearby South Staffordshire increased from 8.1% to 8.8%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership in Stafford increased by 1.0 percentage points

Health in Stafford

In 2021, 48.5% of Stafford residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 46.3% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.5% to 34.5%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Stafford residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.0% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.9% to 3.5%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in good health in Stafford decreased by 1.0 percentage points

Unpaid care in Stafford

In 2021, 5.1% of Stafford residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 8.0% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.6% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.4% in 2011. The proportion of Stafford residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.5% to 2.6%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Stafford (2.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (2.9 percentage points, from 7.4% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Stafford decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Religion in Stafford

In 2021, 36.9% of Stafford residents reported having "No religion", up from 22.8% in 2011. The rise of 14.1 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Stafford. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 22.0% to 32.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 54.3% of people in Stafford described themselves as Christian (down from 67.9%), while 5.4% did not state their religion (down from 6.6% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Stafford residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 122,600 Stafford residents said they were born in England. This represented 89.6% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 118,500 in 2011, which at the time represented 90.5% of Stafford's population.

Wales was the next most represented, with just under 1,800 Stafford residents reporting this country of birth (1.3%). This figure was down from just under 1,900 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.5% of the population of Stafford.

The number of Stafford residents born in Scotland fell from around 1,900 in 2011 (1.4% of the local population) to around 1,700 in 2021 (1.2%).

In 2021, 89.6% of Stafford residents reported their country of birth as England

Change in employment

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in nearby South Staffordshire (4.2 percentage points) than in Stafford (1.0 percentage points).

In Stafford, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) decreased from 57.4% in 2011 to 56.4% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby South Staffordshire decreased from 57.5% to 53.3%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Stafford fell from 2.8% to 2.0%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) increased from 24.7% to 27.2%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Stafford decreased by 1.0 percentage points

Stafford stood out from other areas for working hours

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week fell in Stafford, but rose across England.

In Stafford, the percentage that worked 15 hours or less in a week fell from 10.0% in 2011 to 9.5% in 2021, while across England it rose from 9.7% to 10.3%. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 9.6% to 9.9%.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in Stafford fell from 14.7% to 12.6%, while the percentage of adults in employment who worked 31 to 48 hours increased from 56.0% to 59.6%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Stafford decreased by 0.5 percentage points

Family in Stafford

Of Stafford households, 20.0% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 20.5% in 2011.

This area had the region’s highest percentage of households including a couple but no children. Wychavon had the West Midlands' next highest percentage of households including a couple but no children (19.7%), while Birmingham had the region's lowest percentage (11.5%).

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Stafford decreased by 0.4 percentage points

National identity in Stafford

In 2021, 4.2% of Stafford residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 3.5% in 2011.

In 2021, 1.1% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.4% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Stafford that identified as "British only" increased from 15.6% to 56.4%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the West Midlands (2.5 percentage points, from 6.2% to 8.7%) than in Stafford (0.7 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Stafford increased by 0.7 percentage points

Change in housing in Stafford

Of Stafford households, 70.0% owned their home in 2021, down from 71.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in six households (15.5%) rented privately, compared with 12.9% in 2011. The percentage of Stafford households that lived in a socially rented property decreased from 13.7% to 13.6%.

The decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home was greater across the West Midlands (2.1 percentage points, from 64.9% to 62.8%) than in Stafford (1.6 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.0 percentage points, from 63.3% to 61.3%.

The rate of home ownership in Stafford decreased by 1.6 percentage points

Disability in Stafford

In 2021, 6.7% of Stafford residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 8.0% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under one in nine people (10.6%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 10.2% in 2011. The proportion of Stafford residents who were not disabled increased from 81.8% to 82.7%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater across the West Midlands (1.9 percentage points, from 9.9% to 8.0%) than in Stafford (1.3 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Stafford decreased by 1.3 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Stafford

In 2021, 1.9% of Stafford residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 1.3% in 2011. The 0.6 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 2.4% to 3.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 93.4% of people in Stafford identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 95.0% in 2011), while 3.0% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 2.5% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 0.8% in 2011 to 1.1% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
